The United Arab Emirates is a federation of seven emirates on the south-eastern coast of the Persian Gulf, formed in 1971, with Abu Dhabi as its capital and Dubai as its largest city. The map shows its area from 1945, when it was still the British-protected Trucial States.

Before oil, the coast lived from fishing, trade and pearl diving, and was poor. Oil was found in Abu Dhabi in 1958 and exported from 1962. When Britain announced it would leave the Gulf, the rulers of Abu Dhabi and Dubai agreed to unite. The federation was declared on 2 December 1971 with six emirates; Ras al-Khaimah joined in 1972. Sheikh Zayed of Abu Dhabi was president until his death in 2004.

Abu Dhabi holds most of the oil. Dubai, with less oil, made itself a hub of shipping, flights, finance and tourism, symbolised by the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, opened in 2010. Most residents are foreign workers, many from South Asia, such as the workers from Kerala.
